sentences.text: Kritosaurus is an incompletely known genus of duck-billed dinosaur.
The type specimen consists of a partial skull, lower jaws, and associated postcranial remains.

A partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin in Mexico was described as Kritosaurus sp. but later considered an indeterminate saurolophine. This skeleton is approximately 11 meters long and about 20% larger than other known specimens.
The genus Kritosaurus was described by Brown in 1910, with the type species Kritosaurus navajovius.
Barnum Brown discovered the type specimen in 1904 near the Ojo Alamo Formation in San Juan County, New Mexico.
Fossils have also been found in the Olmos Formation in Mexico.
Kritosaurus was a large bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore that used a grinding motion analogous to chewing.
It had continuously replacing teeth packed into dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a few in use at any time.
Researchers suggest the nasal crest may have been used for social functions like identifying sex, species, or social ranking.
It is hypothesized that inflatable air sacs flanked the crest for visual and auditory signaling.
Barnum Brown synonymized the genus Gryposaurus with Kritosaurus, a classification supported by Charles Gilmore.
Lull and Wright assigned the species Hadrosaurus breviceps to Kritosaurus, but this classification is no longer accepted.

In 1984, José Bonaparte and colleagues named the species Kritosaurus australis based on fossils from Patagonia, Argentina. Further analysis proved that Kritosaurus australis belongs to a new genus, which was named Huallasaurus by Rozadilla et al. in 2022.
Kritosaurus lived approximately 74.5 to 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in North America.
The habitat was interpreted as river floodplains that formed after the retreat of the Western Interior Seaway.
Conifers were the dominant plants in the environment, and chasmosaurine horned dinosaurs were more common than hadrosaurids.
It is debated whether Kritosaurus is a valid genus, as Hunt and Lucas judged it a nomen dubium due to a lack of diagnostic features.
Some authors, including Thomas E. Williamson, defend the interpretation that Anasazisaurus and Kritosaurus are distinct genera.
There is a debate regarding the age of the Kritosaurus holotype because the Ojo Alamo Formation is divided by an unconformity into older Campanian and younger Maastrichtian members.
The taxonomy of Kritosaurus is complicated by its historical association with Gryposaurus, Anasazisaurus, and Naashoibitosaurus, and remains unresolved until better remains are described.
